newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal minister sees steady unemployment in '97.
newsitem.headline: Portugal minister sees steady unemployment in '97.

text.p: Employment Minister Maria Joao Rodrigues said she expected the Portuguese unemployment rate to remain fairly steady this year.

Asked to forecast the trend for unemployment in 1997, she told Reuters in an interview on Friday night: "Macroeconomic forecasts lead us to believe that unemployment could remain stable in Portugal and could stand at 7.2 or 7.3 percent."
Fourth quarter 1996 unemployment was 7.2 percent, according to the latest available figures from the National Statistics Institute (INE).
Rodrigues said Portugal's economic recovery, its progress to boost exports and the general upturn of the world economy would prevent a deterioration in the unemployment rate in 1997.

She said Portugal had a low unemployment rate compared with other European states because it had a low birth rate; people were staying in the education system longer; and it had a relatively high proportion of women in the workforce.
She said that during Portugal's colonial wars, a period of high emigration in the 1960s and 1970s, many Portuguese women took over the jobs of men.
